findings.title: Cleanup ticker interval reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute without justification
findings.body: The cleanup service ticker is changed from time.Minute*10 to time.Minute*1. This is unrelated to splitting the annotation DELETE queries and makes all cleanup jobs, including the annotation scan/delete batches, run 10x more often. On large installations this increases database load and, because a cleanup run can take up to the 9-minute timeout while ticks are buffered, can cause back-to-back cleanup runs. Restore the 10-minute interval unless the change is intentional and justified.

findings.title: Normal cleanup progress is logged at Error level with full ID lists
findings.body: Lines 534, 537, 554, 557, 576 and 579 use r.log.Error for routine, successful batch operations, including when err is nil and when no IDs were found. They also embed the entire ids slice, which can contain tens of thousands of IDs when AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize is large. In production this will flood error logs, trigger error-based alerting for non-errors, and create very large log lines every batch. These messages should be Debug (or Info at most), should not log a nil err as an error, and should log counts rather than full ID lists.

findings.title: deleteByIDs can exceed database bind-parameter limits for non-SQLite databases
findings.body: deleteByIDs builds a single DELETE ... WHERE id IN (?, ?, ...) with one placeholder per fetched ID, and only special-cases SQLite when the configured batch size exceeds 999. AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize is operator-configurable and unbounded here; on PostgreSQL/MySQL a large value (the new test itself uses 32767) can approach or exceed the driver's bind-parameter limit (e.g. 65535 on PostgreSQL), causing cleanup to fail every run, whereas the previous subquery DELETE had no host-parameter limit. Chunk deletes by len(ids) against a safe per-dialect limit instead of relying only on the SQLite/configured-batch-size check.
